at a dilution of 1/2000 in blocking buffer for 45 min. Slides were then washed with PBS, aspirated, and mounted with Fluorosave (Millipore) for imaging. Immunofluorescence images were acquired using an Observer Z1 fluorescent microscope (Carl Zeiss) and exported as .tif files with all channels separate before loading into the Myotally desktop application. Myotally is compatible with both MacOS (Monterey 12.4 or newer) and Windows (Win 10). Note: Images of muscle cross-sections used for input files should be stained for proteins that clearly delineate myofiber borders, such as Laminin or Dystrophin. While Myotally is compatible with various image qualities and common image formats, including .jpg., and .png., we strongly discourage the use of these formats for analysis. These lossy formats do not preserve critical metadata, including the effective pixel size (conversion factor or physical pixel size of the camera divided by total magnification). Without this information, quantification outputs may be inaccurate due to improper pixel-to-micrometer scaling.

steps.title: Dissect and freeze TA muscles
steps.instruction: Harvest injured and uninjured tibialis anterior (TA) muscles from wild‑type mice and freeze them immediately after dissection.

steps.title: Fix and dehydrate RFP‑expressing muscles
steps.instruction: Fix TA muscles that contain RFP‑expressing myofibers in 0.5 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) and then dehydrate them in 20 % sucrose before cryopreservation.

steps.title: Embed in OCT and snap‑freeze
steps.instruction: Embed the muscles in OCT (Fisher) and submerge them in liquid‑nitrogen‑cooled isopentane (Sigma) for 30 seconds to snap‑freeze.

steps.title: Store frozen tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen OCT blocks to a –80 °C freezer for storage until sectioning.

steps.title: Section muscle at mid‑belly
steps.instruction: Cut cryosections through the mid‑belly of each TA muscle at a thickness of 10 µm.

steps.title: Fix sections
steps.instruction: Fix the sections in 2 % PFA at room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Incubate sections overnight at 4 °C in blocking buffer consisting of 2 % BSA and 0.3 % PBS‑Tween (Sigma).

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Add anti‑Laminin primary antibody (Abcam 11576) diluted 1:1000 in the blocking buffer and incubate at room temperature for 2 hours.

steps.title: Wash primary antibody
steps.instruction: Rinse sections with PBS to remove unbound primary antibody.

steps.title: Secondary antibody and DAPI staining
steps.instruction: Incubate sections in blocking buffer containing secondary antibody (Thermo A32744) diluted 1:500 and DAPI (Thermo D1306) diluted 1:2000 for 45 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Final washes and mounting
steps.instruction: Wash sections with PBS, aspirate excess buffer, and mount slides with FluoroSave (Millipore).

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Capture images on an Observer Z1 fluorescent microscope (Carl Zeiss), ensuring each channel (e.g., Laminin, DAPI, RFP) is saved separately as lossless .tif files.

steps.title: Verify pixel scaling
steps.instruction: Confirm the µm/pixel conversion for each image: typical color‑camera pixel sizes are 3–5 µm (effective 0.3–0.15 µm/pixel at 10×–20×), and fluorescence cameras often have 6.5 µm pixels (effective 0.65–0.325 µm/pixel). Record the exact µm/pixel ratio before analysis.

steps.title: Load images into Myotally
steps.instruction: Open the Myotally desktop application (compatible with macOS Monterey 12.4+ or Windows 10), import the .tif files, and verify that the pixel‑size metadata is correctly recognized.

steps.title: Run automatic fiber analysis
steps.instruction: Execute Myotally’s automatic pipeline to quantify myofiber cross‑sectional area (CSA), fiber number, and central nucleation for each image.

steps.title: Optional: quantify fluorescence intensity
steps.instruction: If measuring mean fluorescence intensity (MFI), enable the optional MFI module in Myotally; the software will calculate MFI for each fiber (e.g., RFP in Pax7CreER/tdTomato mice).
